images.name: duties
images.title: The salon booking desk, *duty by duty*
rows: Books the right length, stylist, room and processing time from the salon's own rules.
Books them before the main appointment and moves it if the test wasn't done.
Takes deposits, sends reminders and fills cancellations from the waitlist.
Texts clients past their usual visit gap with times from their stylist's calendar.
Collects the form and sends health details to the therapist before confirming.
Gathers the details and alerts the manager the same day.

images.name: day-on-shift
images.title: A Saturday at a *hair salon*
rows: A client cancels a 10 am cut by text. It offers the time to the waitlist and fills it.
A new colour client never came in for her patch test. It moves her colour to next week and books the test.
A caller wants to fix box dye that went orange. It books a consultation and sends notes to the stylist.
Answers six messages about prices and parking while the desk checks out clients.
A client says Tuesday's toner faded in two days. It alerts the manager with her photos.
Texts 14 clients who are past their usual colour interval with open times.
A client asks to skip the late-cancel fee. It collects the reason for the manager.
Books a balayage and trim for next Saturday, with a deposit.

images.name: setup
images.title: How an AI booking assistant *is set up* at a salon
steps: Length, processing time, consult and patch-test rules for every service.
Their specialties, speed, days and which services they don't do.
Deposits, cancellation fees, waitlist and who decides exceptions.
Calendar, menu, contacts and history. Payment links, never card numbers.
It drafts replies while the manager reads the log, then takes on more.
Update it when stylists, prices or services change.
